claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 and lives with me at home. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm happy to help you determine if you can still claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, the key factor is whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training? For example, is he studying at school, college, or university, or doing an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! A-levels at sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now let me ask about Alex's circumstances:

**Is Alex working at all? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's just focused on his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't claimed any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just one more question to ensure I have all the information I need:

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 years old and studying A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
- Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and Alex lives at home with you, which satisfies the residency and responsibility requirements
- Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week
- Alex has not started claiming benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)

**Important note:** Please be aware that if either you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the government's Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he finishes his A-levels, starts working 24 hours or more per week, or claims benefits in his own right), you should contact HMRC as this could affect your entitlement.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
